He wrote of a god who made all of his subjects conform to their stated moral code, which led to those entities becoming hermits in a tree instead of sublimating their private vices into public benefits. One member of this group is alleged to have been involved in both the "Fair Barn" and "Gotta Go" incidents. This group was linked by the actions of Reed Walters after Justin Barker suffered a concussion, ending a series of events that began when a high school student asked to sit under a tree. For 10 points— identify this group which was given harsher charges than white offenders in a series of reprisal assaults in a Louisiana town.

The Adige River became the line of demarcation between two powers under this treaty, which also established a zone of annexation stretching from Andernach to Basel. Everything taken from Venice by one party to this treaty was later lost at the Treaty of Pressburg. Followed by further chipping away at the Holy Roman Empire in the treaties of Rastatt and Lunéville, its signers recognized the Ligurian and Cisalpine Republics. Ending the War of the First Coalition, it had a secret clause against Prussia. For 10 points— name this 1797 treaty between Napoleonic France and Austria.

Opposition movements in this country include Erk, Birlik and an Islamist group led by the late Juma Namangoniy. In May 2005, hundreds of civilian protestors were shot in this country's Andijan massacre, which was followed by the expulsion of Americans from the Khanabad military base. For 10 points— name this Central Asian country which is a major producer of cotton and is ruled by Islam Karimov.

This group advocated baihua literature over the classical wenyan style and was burned down the house of the communicatiosn minister over the proposed occupation of Shantung. This group grew out of the journal New Youth and the New Culture Movement led by Chen Duxiu and Hu Shih. Its center was colleges in Beijing, whose protest of the Versailles Treaty gave this group its name. For 10 points— identify this nationalist modernizing society of Republican China, named for a date.

The surrender of this man led another king to keep lands up to the Mulucha river. He attempted to kill Hiempsal and Adherbal to take power after the death of Micipsa. This man's father-in-law, the king of Mauritania Bocchus, eventually turned him over after Quintus Metellus had failed to get revenge for this man's massacre at Cirta. For 10 points— name this king of Numidia pursued by Sulla and Marius in a war of the 100s BCE.

One leader of this organization was a Quaker who later resigned from the Gladstone government to protest the war with Egypt. Another important figure in this group went on a world tour and wrote the book England, Ireland, and America. Financed by Samuel Courtauld, this group's leader made a speech which caused Robert Peel to flee the Parliamentary chamber during a debate on the Irish famine. For 10 points— John Bright and Richard Cobden let what group which sought to end import duties on grain?

In one work by this creator of The Triumph of Caesar, a fat black bird, a dark-skinned man with a headdress, and a bunch of flying infants look down through a painted oculus in the ceiling of Camera degla Sposli, found in the Mantuan Ducal Palace. This painter of Agony in the Garden also showed a woman sticking a handkerchief in her left eye on the side of a notably foreshortened corpse. For 10 points — name this painter of Dead Christ.

Sometimes called the "lord of red steeds," this consort of Svaha is responsible for digesting food and holding up heaven with a column. This god has a chariot that is pulled by parrots, and serves priestly functions within the pantheon. Eight books of the Rig Veda open with prayers to this god, is depicted with seven tongues and two faces, covered in ghee. For 10 points— name this Vedic god of fire.

Stuntish acts during this man's term included a walking tour of Sarajevo during the Yugoslavian war and inviting every Nobel laureate to a conference on world problems. He had first become nationally prominent by forcing a runoff in the 1965 presidential election, and later this man dismissed hardliner Pierre Mauroy and appointed the technocrat Laurent Fabius in an attempt to save the economy. His party's loss of control of parliament in the late 1980s led to his "cohabitation" with Jacques Chirac. For 10 points— name this Socialist President of France.

In one of this man's writings, the fable of the Trogolodytes is told by Usbek to Mirza. He identified virtue, honor, and fear as the motivating principles of different forms of government. He also said that climate determined politics, and this author of the Persian Letters advocated the separation of powers in his major work. For 10 points— name this author The Spirit of the Laws.
Charles-Louis de Secondat, baron de La Brède et de Montesquieu

This man replaced Fernando Wood as the leader of his organization, he is shown as a a vulture overlooking skulls and bones labeled "law" and "treasury" in one notable portrait, and raising a club as he takes two children by the collar in another. Opposed by newspaper publisher George Jones and governor Samuel Tilden, he escaped from prison and was captured in Cuba thanks to the efforts of Thomas Nast. For 10 points— name this infamous leader of Tammany Hall.

He battled for a starting job with Trent Dilfer in the year after Dilfer won a Super Bowl. This Boston College alum spent two years as a Brett Favre backup before landing a job where Deion Branch, Nate Burleson, and Bobby Engram are his common targets. For 10 points— name this man who wants the ball because we're going to score, the quarterback for the Seattle Seahawks.

One person who held this post was the grandson and namesake of the 1860s minister to England and unsuccessful Free Soil Party Vice Presidential candidate, Charles Francis Adams. Also held by the unfortunate Abel Upshur, its notable Civil War occupant was Gideon Wells. Prior to becoming the first Secretary of Defense, James Forrestal had this job. For 10 points— name this former Cabinet-level position.

For the first two years of its rule, this group his the identities of its leaders, using names such as "Brother Number Three" and the Angka. Ta Mok led a coup to gain control of this group in 1997, eighteen years after it lost power due to a Vietnamese invasion following its uneasy alliance with Norodom Sihanouk. For 10 points— name this Pol Pot-led group which instigated a reign of terror in Camodia.

Some of the last areas to join this group were admitted via the Convention of Gastein, and the Heppenheim program and the Vormarz movements attempted to democratize this organization. Governed by a Bundesrat, it implemented the ideas of Friedrich List. Members adopted the metric system and the Vereinsthaler currency. Name this economic union, a precursor to German unification.

Her criticism of European playwrights was published as The Social Significance of the Modern Drama, and this editor of Mother Earth also wrote about the Krondstadt rebellion, which she saw firsthand, in My Disillusionment in Russia. This former partner of would-be assassin Alexander Berkman was in Russia because she had been deported in the Red Scare. For 10 points— name this anarchist.

Those who are not allowed to practice this are known as "muqallids" or "imitators" because they are bound by "taqlid." Methods such as qiyas, or analogy, and ijma, or consensus, were once ways to do it. Sunnis have declared since the fourth Islamic century that the "gates" of this are closed, though Shia still recognize "mujtahids." For 10 points— name this practice of putting forth new interpretations of Sharia law.

He originally named a place he found the Island of the True Cross, though his patron King Manuel changed the name later. Frosty relations with the zamorin of Calicut led to the second tragedy of his expedition, after a storm at the Cape of Good Hope that killed his lieutenant Bartolomeu Dias. For 10 points— name this discoverer of Brazil, a Portuguese sailor who followed Vasco da Gama to India.
